To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the fragmentation pattern of positive ions is determined by the sequential loss of both ligands and/or carboxylate groups from the complexes, and that the fragmentation pattern for the negative ions is determined by a resonant process close to 0eV.
the electron interaction with copper carboxylic complexes is dominated by dissociative electron attachment (DEA) and dissociative electron ionization (DEI) processes.

the electron interaction with the copper carboxylates leads to the production of Cu2(O2C2F5)5−, Cu2(OCCF3)5−, and Cu2(OCCCF3)5− anionic clusters, which are formed by sequential addition of the O2CCF3, O2CCF2, or O2CCF radicals to the Cu2(OCC2F5)n− anions.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the electron impact dissociation of copper(II) coordination complexes.
the interaction of low-energy electrons with the copper(II) complexes containing the carboxylates and amines ligands.
the electron interaction with the copper carboxylates.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the electron interaction with copper(2+) carboxylates is governed by the electron affinity and electron impact ionization energy of the metal ion and the electron affinity of the ligands.
DEA is a more efficient fragmentation pathway than the dissociation of positive ions.
the fragmentation pattern of copper carboxylates in the DEA processes is dominated by the ligands, and the metal center has little impact on the fragmentation pattern.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the electron impact on the copper carboxylates leads to the formation of Cu+ ions, Cu2(OH)2(O2CCF2CF2CF2)4−•, Cu2(OOCCF2CF3)4−• and Cu2(O2CCH3)4− anions.
the electron collision processes with copper carboxylic compounds are dominated by single electron transfer processes, which are followed by dissociation.
the electron impact processes of copper(II) complexes are dominated by the fragmentation of the carboxylates and the amine molecules.
The main takeaway from our work is that
electron impact ionization is a very effective tool in studying the molecular properties of copper carboxylates.
the fragmentation pattern is very similar for all investigated compounds, and the main difference between the complexes lies in the relative intensities of the DEA fragments.
the fragmentation pattern of these complexes is very similar to that of other carboxylate and amine ligands, and that the DEA processes are dominated by the ligands rather than the metal center.
